note: The two sets are nearly identical in content and share the same defects: a misread 0.18 Hz tower frequency that conflicts with the stated 0.170 Hz, an invented 'steady-state' condition, duplicated claims (first tower-monopile mode and the 0.10–0.13 Hz wave range), and 1P/3P ranges whose quotes are only legend labels. A is marginally more faithful: it keeps the 'designed in WISDEM and OpenFAST' condition on the material claim and gives a clean verbatim quote for the 0.17 Hz figure reading, whereas B appends a fabricated bracketed annotation ('[vertical line at ~0.17]') to its quote. Otherwise the correct material, geometry and frequency claims are the same in both.
remarks: Both sets miss notable page facts: the 7% outfitting mass allowance and 100 t transition piece mass, the note that a floating/semisubmersible substructure requires a stiffer tower and shifted frequency requirements, and the soil modeled as spring constants representative of dense sand/gravel. Both state the first tower-monopile mode twice (0.170 Hz) and also give 0.18 Hz for the same quantity from the figure — internally inconsistent; the text value is 0.170 Hz. The 1P (0.09–0.13 Hz) and 3P (0.25–0.38 Hz) ranges and the wave-peak/Wind-PSD values are chart readings not stated in the text, and their quotes are legend labels only. Table 4-1 lists the unit of Poisson's ratio as 'Pa', a typo in the source; neither set propagated it.
